patient_information: A 37-year-old woman from the Lower Shire Valley in southern Malawi.
chief_complaint: She has vomited blood three times over the past 24 hours.
history_of_present_illness: The blood is bright red in colour with no epigastric pain or previous history of vomiting. There is no history of fever or abnormal bleeding and her stool has been normal in colour. She had not taken any regular painkillers and did not drink any alcohol before symptoms began.
exposure_and_epidemiology: She lives and works on a large sugar plantation in the area, is married with three children, all well, and had a negative HIV test 3 months prior. The region is highly endemic for schistosomiasis, with virtually all water bodies infested with Schistosoma mansoni and S. haematobium.
vitals: Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, pulse 110bpm, respiratory rate 28 breath cycles per minute, and she is afebrile.
physical_exam: She is slim but not wasted, with slightly pale conjunctivae, no subconjunctival effusions, and no jaundice. Abdomen has no distension or tenderness. The spleen is palpable at 10cm below the left costal margin, the liver is slightly enlarged without stigmata of chronic liver disease, no shifting dullness, no peripheral oedema, and no enlarged lymph nodes. The rest of the physical examination is normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results showed WBC 2.8 x 10^9/L (reference 4-10), Haemoglobin 8.3 g/dL (reference 12-14), MCV 88 fL (reference 80-99), and Platelets 130 x 10^9/L (reference 150-400), indicating pancytopenia with normocytic anaemia. An HIV test 3 months prior was negative. Endoscopy confirmed oesophageal varices, Hepatitis B and C serologies were negative, and one stool sample for S. mansoni ova was negative. Ultrasound of the liver showed a pattern typical of pipestem fibrosis.
differential_diagnosis: Portal hypertension and gastro-oesophageal varices are most likely. Other less likely causes include peptic ulcer disease, erosive gastritis, bleeding tumour, oesophageal cancer, and visceral leishmaniasis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient received IV fluids, underwent endoscopy where oesophageal varices were confirmed and banded, and received a single dose of praziquantel 40 mg/kg. She was discharged home.
